customer_question: The referenced Controller QDID has LMP 31/1 marked as Mandatory. When we enter RF 1/1:YES (Class 1) in the ICS, we get an error. Why? And what is the correct RF Class setting?
question_variants: LMP 31/1 Mandatory error when RF 1/1:YES — what does this mean?
What RF Power Class should we register when the Controller QDID requires specific LMP ICS settings?
RF Class 1 vs Class 2 — when is Class 2 required even if the hardware is Class 1?
actual_issue: The customer's product uses an IC that is Class 1 capable, and they initially entered RF 1/1:YES (Class 1 = output power > +10 dBm) in the ICS. However, the referenced Controller QDID has LMP 31/1 (Power Control) marked as Mandatory. If RF 1/1:YES (Class 1), then LMP 31/1 is triggered as Mandatory — but the product does not implement Power Control. This causes a Consistency Check failure that cannot be resolved without either implementing Power Control or changing to RF Class 2.
plain_english_explanation: In Bluetooth, if a device declares Class 1 output power (RF 1/1:YES), the ICS mandates that it also implements Power Control (LMP 31/1:YES). This is because Class 1 devices, which transmit at higher power, must be able to reduce their power when requested — otherwise they could overwhelm nearby receivers. The referenced Controller QDID declares LMP 31/1 as Mandatory. If the product does not actually implement Power Control but is operating at Class 2 levels, the solution is to register as RF Class 2 (RF 1/1:NO). The actual RF PHY output can still be declared as Class 1 capable (RF PHY 1/15:YES), as long as the LL layer declares Class 2.
consultant_answer: Change RF registration to Class 2 (RF 1/1:NO). This resolves the LMP 31/1 Mandatory conflict. If the RF PHY hardware is capable of Class 1 output, you can still declare RF PHY 1/15:YES to show the full hardware capability, but the LL layer must declare Class 2 to avoid triggering the Power Control mandatory requirement. The product should operate at Class 2 levels during actual use.
decision_logic: RF 1/1:YES (Class 1 at LL layer) → LMP 31/1:YES mandatory → cannot pass Consistency Check if Power Control is not implemented. RF 1/1:NO (Class 2 at LL layer) → LMP 31/1 condition not triggered → Consistency Check passes. RF PHY 1/15 (hardware Class 1 capability) is independent of LL Class declaration.
final_recommendation: When referencing a Controller QDID that has LMP 31/1 Mandatory, set LL-layer RF Class to Class 2 (RF 1/1:NO) unless the product actually implements Power Control. The RF PHY layer can still declare hardware Class 1 capability (RF PHY 1/15:YES) separately.
risk_if_done_wrong: Declaring Class 1 at the LL layer without implementing Power Control causes a Consistency Check failure and blocks registration submission. If the ICS is falsified to pass, this constitutes a qualification error that may lead to SIG challenge.
